post.caption: Locket once meant a window bar. It comes from French loquet, meaning a latch or bolt. In the 1300s it meant an iron bar fastening a window. The little hinged case is first recorded in the late 1600s. Lockets grew out of hinged pendants that held holy relics. Elizabeth I's locket ring from about 1575 hides two portraits. The Heneage Jewel is a locket holding a miniature of the queen. By about 1850, daguerreotype portraits sat inside lockets. Soon lockets paired a photograph with a lock of hair. A hinge on one side and a small catch opposite close it.
